content:
riley: heads-up from onboarding: our quickstart sample shows request identifier sometimes missing after an auth retry. repro is flaky locally but consistent when NODE_DEBUG=1 and TELEMETRY_OTEL=1.
tomas: do you mean the header is gone or the logger/span doesn't show it? can you paste a log + headers?
riley: captured sequence below:
IN: headers={"x-request-id":"rid-2026-abc"} path=/v1/chat
LOG: info handling request request_id=<masked>
OUT (retry): outgoing headers={} status=200
so header arrives, logger prints masked value, and outgoing retry drops the header.
priya: interesting. masking vs dropping are two different things. which SDK versions? any custom redaction rules?
riley: node sdk@2.4.1 in sampleapp, python sdk@1.11.0 in the other repo. REDWOOD_REDACT_LEVEL=medium, SDK_LOG_AUTOINIT=1, AUTH_RETRIES=2.
nadia: parity note: node uses async_hooks to keep context; python uses contextvars. import-time logger install can clobber contextvar defaults. this will cause the tracing/reqid binding to be lost on subsequent attempts.
tomas: sounds like an init-order race: the logger autoinit installs a non-context-aware handler during module import so when telemetry later binds reqid it never gets wired into the logger. then retry code creates a fresh request without copying the original header.
priya: short-term mitigation: retry layer should be defensive and copy X-Request-Id from the original attempt if present. that buys time while we fix init ordering.
riley: agreed. i can add a tiny shim in the retry middleware that does: if (!headers["x-request-id"]) headers["x-request-id"] = attemptContext.headers["x-request-id"];
priya: long-term: we should add an init contract: telemetry.register() must run before logger autoinit. maybe export a function redwood.init({ telemetryFirst: true }) or set REDWOOD_INIT_ORDER=telemetry_first.
nadia: alternative safer approach: make telemetry hook idempotent and bind reqid into a globally accessible token provider that logging autoinit reads from at install time. then even if install order is reversed, the logger can look up provider for current request id. this avoids forcing order changes.
tomas: testing: add cross-runtime unit that simulates 401->retry and asserts header preserved for both node and python. add an e2e in docker-compose that toggles SDK_LOG_AUTOINIT on/off to show the difference.
priya: redaction nuance: our scrubber currently runs on any key that matches /req|token/i and replaces with <masked>. that's fine for user payloads but we must never scrub internal tracing ids. propose whitelist env REDWOOD_REDACT_WHITELIST=x-request-id,request-id. default includes common tracing keys.
riley: i'll open a PR with: (1) retry header-copy shim, (2) unit + e2e repro (node + python), (3) docs for REDWOOD_INIT_ORDER and REDWOOD_REDACT_WHITELIST, (4) opt-in telemetryFirst flag in redwood.init.
priya: please note in the PR description the risk of breaking changes for customers who relied on current autoinit behaviour. include migration steps and a feature-flag gated rollout.
nadia: QA tips: run sampleapp with SDK_LOG_AUTOINIT=1 and then with 0, compare trace ids, and run with REDWOOD_REDACT_WHITELIST unset vs set. add a flaky-tolerance tag to tests since this repro can vary with timing.
deploy-bot: infra: created issue INF-903 "preserve-request-id-across-retries + telemetry init ordering" assigned to devex, priority=p1
tomas: thanks. after PR lands we should coordinate a canary release and monitor staging traces for drop rate. riley: include a short reproduction script so support can help customers who hit this during onboarding.
riley: will do, opening PR now and pinging the thread when CI completes. thanks all! :pray:
